summary_paragraph: An elderly female with a history of chronic diastolic heart failure, recurrent pulmonary emboli on anticoagulation, chronic chest pain, and microcytic anemia presented with left-sided chest pain, bilateral leg swelling, and mild abdominal pain. The chest pain was reproducible on palpation of the neck and shoulder, with normal EKG and troponins, making acute cardiac ischemia unlikely. Chest X-ray showed stable mild-to-moderate pulmonary edema and bilateral pleural effusions. She received IV furosemide for volume overload, with improvement in edema and oxygenation. Abdominal pain resolved spontaneously, with normal liver and pancreatic enzymes. Acetaminophen was added for musculoskeletal pain control. She was discharged home the following day in stable condition with continued management of her chronic conditions and follow-up planned with her primary care provider.
